event.what_happened: October 2026 data showed retail sales growth of 0.4% year over year, fixed-asset investment down 8.1% for January to October, and property development investment down 21.6%.
event.how_it_reaches_markets: Weaker demand for commodities and for foreign companies selling into China; pressure on Chinese and Hong Kong shares; deflationary pressure exported through cheap goods, which also feeds the tariff dispute.

sourced_facts.text: October 2026: value added of industry above designated size +4.8% y/y; retail sales of consumer goods +0.4% y/y (National Bureau of Statistics, released 2026-11-16)
September 2026, for comparison: industry +5.5% y/y; retail sales +1.1% y/y (National Bureau of Statistics, released 2026-10-19)
January to October 2026: fixed-asset investment -8.1% y/y; real estate development investment -21.6% y/y (National Bureau of Statistics)

history.note: Card opened. Resolution conditions written before the outcome is known.

unconfirmed_facts: Week ending 2026-11-20: Hang Seng -5.19%, CSI 300 -1.54%: from a fund manager's weekly note; not confirmed at a primary or wire source

notes: Retail sales and property investment are read from the monthly National Bureau of Statistics release. 'Large' default means a public bond of at least $100 million equivalent.

items.measure: Retail sales growth above 3.0% year over year in 3 monthly releases in a row
Year-to-date property development investment down by less than 10.0%
Retail sales growth below 0.0% year over year in any monthly release
A default on a public bond of at least $100 million equivalent by a developer or local-government financing vehicle: 1 case is enough

counter_view.text: China's property slump is several years old and the US market has lived with it. Industrial output still grew 4.8% in October. This may stay a slow drag that never turns into a US market event.

worsened_when_any: Retail sales fall year over year
A large developer or local-government financing vehicle defaults on a public bond
